title: LoRAHub over Mirror-compressed candidate basis
hypothesis: For candidate LoRA updates that share a Givens-conjugacy orbit, one rank-2 physical adapter basis plus one angle per candidate can preserve few-shot signed LoRAHub composition quality with fewer bytes than the full candidate bank and outperform a scalar shared-basis control; unrelated candidates should require private modules.
physical_object: one rank-2 16x16 adapter basis versus eight independently trained candidate LoRA updates
mirror_coordinate: one Givens angle per candidate; each candidate update is a conjugated view of the shared rank-2 update
logical_multiplicity: eight candidate LoRA modules composed into four few-shot target task updates

model.composition: four fixed signed mixtures of the same eight candidate updates; infer composition coefficients from 32 support examples by ridge least squares

controls: LoRAHub reference: all eight independent rank-2 candidate modules, with signed few-shot composition
one shared rank-2 basis plus one direct scalar per candidate
one shared rank-2 basis plus one Givens angle per candidate
hard-shared single rank-2 update with no candidate code
development_gate_before_fresh: For the aligned condition in both seeds: full-bank target test MSE <1e-4; Mirror target MSE <=1.10x full-bank and <=0.80x scalar shared basis; actual Mirror bytes <=0.60x full bank; and Mirror source-task residuals finite. Report unrelated condition as a boundary test; fresh remains sealed if aligned gate fails.
success_gate: All three fresh aligned worlds meet the registered quality and byte gates; unrelated candidate condition shows and records any private-capacity requirement; include one-time decode MACs and few-shot search cost; exact reload/replay.
failure_gate: Mirror misses aligned-condition quality or byte gate in both development seeds, or scalar matches within the registered quality margin.

storage.authority: actual deterministic ZIP/NPY FP16 inference payload bytes after reload
paid_objects: independent LoRA A/B factors or shared basis factors

boundaries: synthetic linear low-rank task bank only; no NLP or LoRAHub benchmark claim
target mixture count is fixed across methods and not counted as Mirror capacity
aligned and unrelated candidate families are both preregistered; do not tune on fresh
fixed-update result is learning-efficiency evidence, not a near-converged capacity result
fresh IDs remain sealed until aligned development gates pass
